title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: All database interactions use Django ORM methods (get, get_or_create) with bound parameters; no raw SQL or string interpolation is performed.

The endpoint accepts a user-controlled rule_id from the URL and fetches the rule without verifying that the rule belongs to the specified project or that the user has explicit permission to mute that rule. This could allow a user to snooze rules in other projects or unassigned rules across the organization, potentially violating intended authorization boundaries.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a check that the fetched rule's project matches the project from the URL (e.g., if isinstance(rule, Rule): assert rule.project_id == project.id). Also ensure that the user has explicit permission to mute the rule, possibly by verifying ownership or project-level permissions before allowing snooze. This prevents IDOR and enforces proper authorization.
